summary: Use FSRS-6, not SM-2/Leitner/WaniKani stages. FSRS-6 is Anki's shipped default (since Anki 25.07), its default parameters are fit on ~727M real reviews, and it is a pure function of three numbers per card (stability, difficulty, retrievability) — roughly 120 lines of arithmetic with no server and no training required. I ported it to plain dependency-free ES-module JavaScript and differential-tested it against the real `ts-fsrs` npm package (v5.4.2, FSRS-6.0, MIT): 36,000 random state transitions across 5 parameter configurations, fuzz on and off, 0 mismatches on every card field and every review-log field. The 21-weight default vector is verified identical in three independent sources (ts-fsrs `constant.ts`, Rust `fsrs-rs/src/inference_v6.rs`, and the awesome-fsrs wiki). FSRS-7 exists in `fsrs-rs` main as a 34-parameter model but is not the shipped default anywhere and has no TS reference implementation — do not use it. Beyond the scheduler, the important design calls are: "learn words" is a non-SRS first-exposure flow that ends by seeding the card with a real FSRS rating; a single unified `cards` store with deck *tags* rather than separate per-level databases; sibling burying keyed on a shared `noteId` so a word, its kanji and its sentence never appear in the same session; and a conservative default card-type set (JP→EN only at N5, adding EN→JP production and kanji→reading from N4/N3, cloze at N2/N1).

recommendations.title: Ship FSRS-6 with the official default weight vector, not SM-2
recommendations.decision: Implement FSRS-6 exactly as in the `code_or_data` module. Hard-code the 21-weight default `[0.212, 1.2931, 2.3065, 8.2956, 6.4133, 0.8334, 3.0194, 0.001, 1.8722, 0.1666, 0.796, 1.4835, 0.0614, 0.2629, 1.6483, 0.6014, 1.8729, 0.5425, 0.0912, 0.0658, 0.1542]` with `request_retention: 0.9`, `maximum_interval: 36500`, `enable_short_term: true`, `enable_fuzz: true`, `learning_steps: ['1m','10m']`, `relearning_steps: ['10m']`. Do NOT attempt on-device parameter optimisation in v1.
recommendations.why: FSRS-6 is Anki's default since 25.07 and needs ~20-30% fewer reviews than SM-2 for the same retention. The defaults were fit on ~727M reviews from ~10k users, so an untrained solo learner already gets near-optimal scheduling on day one. Implementation risk is near zero: it is closed-form arithmetic with no state beyond (stability, difficulty, last_review). I verified my port is bit-identical to ts-fsrs over 36,000 transitions. Optimisation (FSRS-rs gradient descent) needs ~1,000+ reviews before it beats the defaults and would mean shipping a WASM trainer — not worth it for v1.

recommendations.title: Do not use FSRS-7, WaniKani stages, Leitner, or jpdb's model
recommendations.decision: Reject the alternatives explicitly. FSRS-7 (34 params, `fsrs-rs/src/inference_v7.rs`) is unreleased-as-default and has no TypeScript/JS reference — revisit only when ts-fsrs ships it. WaniKani-style fixed stages (4h/8h/1d/3d/1w/2w/1mo/4mo) and Leitner boxes are 5x simpler but ignore per-card difficulty and elapsed time, so a card answered 60 days late is treated like one answered on time. jpdb's scheduler is closed-source and unspecifiable.
recommendations.why: Fixed-stage systems are only attractive when you cannot compute; here the computation is 120 lines. Their failure mode is exactly the one a phone-app learner hits: irregular study and long gaps. FSRS handles elapsed-time deviation natively via the retrievability term.

recommendations.title: Expose retention as one slider labelled in plain language, not as parameters
recommendations.decision: One setting per deck: 'How well do you want to remember?' mapped to `request_retention` — 0.85 'Fast, looser', 0.90 'Balanced' (default), 0.95 'Exam-tight'. Never show w[0..20] in the UI. Show the four button intervals on the card ('Again 10m / Hard 3d / Good 5d / Easy 9d') from `repeat()`, which returns all four outcomes in one call.
recommendations.why: Explainability to a solo learner is the one place FSRS loses to Leitner, and previewing the four intervals recovers all of it — the learner sees the consequence of each button before pressing. Measured with my port: at R=0.90 the all-Good ladder is 10m -> 2d -> 11d -> 46d -> 163d -> 498d; at R=0.85 it is 10m -> 4d -> 31d -> 174d -> 776d. R=0.85 roughly halves workload but the intervals get aggressive fast; 0.90 is the right default and Anki calls it 'the most important setting in FSRS'.

recommendations.title: One unified `cards` store with deck tags, not five per-level databases
recommendations.decision: Single IndexedDB object store `cards` keyed by `id = noteId + ':' + cardType`. Deck membership is an indexed array field `decks: ['N5','saved','business']`. A card can be in a level deck and the saved-words deck simultaneously and still has exactly ONE memory state. Saving a word from a video adds 'saved' to `decks` (and creates the card if absent) — it never clones it.
recommendations.why: The user's saved-words deck necessarily overlaps the level decks (they will save an N4 word while watching an N4 video). Cloning would give the same word two independent schedules and double the reviews. One card, many deck tags, is what makes 'save it for later' composable with the level decks.

recommendations.title: Gate new cards, never gate reviews
recommendations.decision: Per-day limits: `newPerDay` default 20 (offer 10/20/40 presets), `maxReviewsPerDay` default 200. Count against a local-midnight day-rollover hour of 4am (`dayStart = 4`). Build the queue as: all due learning/relearning cards first (they are minute-scale), then reviews (oldest-due first), then up to `newPerDay` new cards interleaved every Nth position so new words are spread through the session, not dumped at the front.
recommendations.why: These are Anki's verified defaults, read from `ankitects/anki/rslib/src/deckconfig/mod.rs`: `new_per_day: 20`, `reviews_per_day: 200`, `learn_steps: [1.0, 10.0]`, `relearn_steps: [10.0]`, `maximum_review_interval: 36_500`, `desired_retention: 0.9`. The 4am rollover matters on a phone: late-night study should count as the previous day.

recommendations.title: Handle backlog by capping the session, not by rescheduling
recommendations.decision: If `dueCount > maxReviewsPerDay`, show a banner ('You have 430 cards waiting — doing 200 today') and serve the 200 oldest-due. Add an explicit 'Catch-up mode' that raises the review cap to unlimited and sets `newPerDay = 0` until the backlog clears. Never bulk-postpone or bulk-rewrite due dates: FSRS already handles overdue cards correctly, and an overdue card answered Good gets a LONGER next interval because low retrievability at recall proves high stability.
recommendations.why: The classic failure of a phone learner is a 2-week gap producing a 900-card wall and app abandonment. Capping the session preserves the memory model (the extra elapsed days are free information for FSRS) while capping the emotional load. Bulk-rescheduling destroys that information.

recommendations.title: Leeches: tag at 8 lapses, do not auto-suspend
recommendations.decision: When `card.lapses >= 8`, set `card.leech = true` and surface it in a 'Trouble words' list; do not remove it from the queue. Offer three one-tap actions on a leech: (a) 'Show me this in a sentence' — switch the card's primary type to a cloze/sentence card, (b) 'Add a mnemonic' — free-text field stored on the note, (c) 'Suspend'. Optionally auto-suspend at 16 lapses.
recommendations.why: Anki's verified default is `leech_threshold: 8` with `leech_action: TagOnly`. Auto-suspending silently deletes the words a learner most needs. For Japanese specifically, a leech is usually a context problem (e.g. an abstract word like 場合 or a kanji-pair confusion like 待つ/持つ), and re-presenting it inside a sentence is the actual fix.

recommendations.title: Sibling burying via a shared noteId, defaulted ON
recommendations.decision: Every card carries `noteId` (the vocabulary entry, e.g. `vocab:食べる`). Kanji cards carry `noteId` of the kanji plus `relatedNotes: ['vocab:食べる', ...]`. When a card is answered, push every other card sharing its `noteId` (and, if `buryRelated` is on, its `relatedNotes`) to `buriedUntil = nextDayStart`. Bury both new and review siblings by default — the opposite of Anki's defaults (`bury_new: false`, `bury_reviews: false`).
recommendations.why: Anki defaults burying off for historical/perf reasons; for Japanese it should be on. Seeing 食べる JP→EN, then EN→JP, then the 食 kanji card, then the cloze sentence all in one session is not four retrievals — it is one retrieval plus three freebies, which inflates stability estimates and wastes session time. Same-day sibling exposure is the single biggest accuracy leak in multi-card Japanese decks.

recommendations.title: Make 'learn words' a distinct non-SRS first-exposure flow that seeds the card
recommendations.decision: 'Learn words' presents batches of 5 new words with NO grading pressure: screen 1 shows word + reading + furigana + meaning + an example sentence + audio, with a 'Next' button; after 5 words, run an immediate low-stakes quiz over just those 5 (multiple-choice 1-of-4 meanings, then a free reading check). The FIRST FSRS rating is written only at the end of that mini-quiz and is derived, not asked: got it first try with no hesitation -> Easy(4); got it -> Good(3); needed a second look -> Hard(2); got it wrong -> Again(1). From then on the card lives in 'flashcards' (review) with the standard 4-button UI. Do not call `schedule()` during the reading-only screens.
recommendations.why: This is the difference between the two menu items the user asked for, and it also fixes FSRS's weakest point: the first review seeds stability directly from the rating (`S0(g) = w[g-1]`, i.e. Again -> 0.212d, Hard -> 1.2931d, Good -> 2.3065d, Easy -> 8.2956d) and difficulty from `D0(g) = w4 - e^((g-1)*w5) + 1`. Verified with my port: a new card rated Easy jumps straight to State.Review with a 9-day interval and D=1.0, skipping learning steps entirely. A garbage first rating therefore poisons the card for weeks. Deriving it from an actual quiz response is far more reliable than asking a beginner 'was that easy?' about a word they met 4 seconds ago.

recommendations.title: Learning steps: 1m / 10m, relearning 10m — and treat them as within-session, not timers
recommendations.decision: Keep `learning_steps: ['1m','10m']` and `relearning_steps: ['10m']`. On a phone, do NOT make the user wait: if a learning card's due time is within the current session, re-queue it after ~4 other cards rather than by wall clock. The scheduler math is unaffected (FSRS uses whole elapsed DAYS; same-day re-reviews take the short-term stability path `S' = S * S^-w19 * e^(w17*(g-3+w18))`).
recommendations.why: Anki's verified defaults are `[1.0, 10.0]` and `[10.0]` minutes. A 10-minute literal wait is fatal on mobile where sessions are 5 minutes long. Because `dayDiff()` returns 0 for any same-day review, re-showing at +90 seconds instead of +10 minutes produces identical FSRS state — only the queue order changes.

recommendations.title: Card types for Japanese, phased by level
recommendations.decision: Define five types: `recognition` (JP word + furigana -> EN meaning), `production` (EN meaning + context hint -> type/recall the JP word), `reading` (kanji word, no furigana -> the kana reading), `audio` (TTS/recorded audio -> meaning), `cloze` (example sentence with the word blanked -> fill it). Defaults per level: N5 = recognition only (+ audio on, it is cheap and high-value). N4 = recognition + reading. N3 = recognition + reading + cloze. N2/N1 = recognition + reading + cloze + audio; leave `production` OFF by default at every level but offer it as a per-deck toggle. Turn `production` ON by default for the Business/Professional decks. All types share one `noteId` so burying applies.
recommendations.why: Recognition is what JLPT actually tests and what unlocks reading/video comprehension — the user's stated fast path. Production cards are 3-5x harder and multiply the review load, which is why jpdb and WaniKani do not force EN->JP recall for vocabulary; they are worth it only when the goal shifts to speaking/writing, i.e. exactly the professional/workplace stage the user described. `reading` becomes essential from N4 where furigana-free kanji compounds start dominating. `cloze` from N3 is where collocation and particle usage (which grammar cards alone do not teach) starts to matter.

recommendations.title: Log every review immutably for later FSRS optimisation
recommendations.decision: Append-only `reviewLogs` store, never updated or deleted, with `{id, cardId, noteId, deck, cardType, rating, state, elapsedDays, lastElapsedDays, scheduledDays, stabilityBefore, difficultyBefore, reviewedAt, durationMs, source}`. Add an 'Export review history' button producing the Anki-compatible CSV (`card_id, review_time, review_rating, review_state, review_duration`) that `fsrs-rs`/`fsrs-optimizer` consumes.
recommendations.why: FSRS optimisation is done offline from exactly this log; the fields mirror ts-fsrs's `ReviewLog` (I verified my log output matches it field-for-field). `durationMs` is required by FSRS-rs's newer cost model and by load-balancing features. Logging it from day one costs nothing and makes personalised parameters possible in v2 without asking the user to start over.

recommendations.title: Undo must restore the previous card state from the log, not re-run the scheduler
recommendations.decision: Keep an in-memory stack of `{cardBefore, logId}` for the current session. Undo writes `cardBefore` back and deletes the log row. Never try to invert `schedule()`.
recommendations.why: FSRS is not invertible (difficulty mean-reversion and fuzz both lose information). A mistapped 'Again' on a 6-month card is the most common real complaint in SRS apps, and on a phone with 4 large buttons it will happen often.

recommendations.title: Bury/suspend semantics and a 'video-saved' inbox
recommendations.decision: `buriedUntil: timestamp` (skip in queue until then) vs `suspended: boolean` (never queued until manually unsuspended; preserves stability/difficulty). Words tapped inside the video player go into `decks: ['saved']` with `state: New` and `suspended: false` but flagged `unreviewed: true`, and appear in a 'New from videos' tray that feeds the 'learn words' flow — do not inject them straight into the review queue.
recommendations.why: A word tapped mid-video has zero first exposure; dropping it into flashcards means the first rating is Again and the card starts at S=0.212d. Routing it through the learn-words flow gives it a proper seed. The tray also gives the user the satisfying 'I collected 12 words from that video' loop that drives retention in apps like jpdb and Migaku.

recommendations.title: Deck mixing: one global queue, weighted, with a per-deck new-card budget
recommendations.decision: Build one merged queue across all active decks. Learning/relearning cards are never deck-filtered (they are time-critical). New-card budget splits by an explicit per-deck `newPerDay` (e.g. N5: 15, saved: 5, business: 0) so the current level deck stays the spine and saved words top it up. Provide a 'Study only this deck' mode from each level screen for focused sessions, but make the home-screen 'Review' button run the merged queue.
recommendations.why: Separate per-deck queues force the user to remember to open five screens, and they will not. A merged queue with a per-deck NEW budget gives level structure where it matters (intake) and one button where it matters (review).

recommendations.title: Nice-to-have: load balancing and 'easy days'
recommendations.decision: After `nextInterval()` returns `i`, search ±15% of `i` for the day with the fewest already-scheduled cards and pick it (only for `i >= 7`). Let the user mark weekdays as light.
recommendations.why: Fuzz alone (±5-15%, already in the module) prevents clumping but does not actively flatten the calendar. Load balancing is the single most-installed Anki add-on behaviour and it materially reduces the '180-card Tuesday' that kills streaks. Cheap to add once you index cards by due-date.

The plain-JS module in code_or_data is numerically identical to the real ts-fsrs scheduler.

verified_facts.claim: FSRS-6 is Anki's shipped default scheduler and FSRS-7 is not yet released as a default.
verified_facts.evidence: Web search of Anki release notes: FSRS became opt-in in Anki 23.10 and the default in Anki 25.07 (July 2025); ~20-30% fewer reviews than SM-2 for the same retention; default parameters fit on ~727M reviews from ~10k users. Separately, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-spaced-repetition/fsrs-rs/main/src/inference_v7.rs does contain `pub static DEFAULT_PARAMETERS: [f32; 34]` (FSRS-7, with a second `stability_fast` memory trace), but ts-fsrs v5.4.2 still reports `using FSRS-6.0` and there is no JS reference implementation of v7.

verified_facts.claim: Real interval ladders produced by the module (all-Good, no fuzz), for UI copy and sanity.
verified_facts.evidence: R=0.90: +10m -> 2d -> 11d -> 46d -> 163d -> 498d -> 1348d -> 3299d. R=0.85: +10m -> 4d -> 31d -> 174d -> 776d -> 2870d -> 9107d. After 4x Good: S=46.32 D=2.10 ivl=46d; then Again: S drops to 2.934, D rises to 7.39, state becomes Relearning, due +10min, lapses=1.

verified_facts.claim: Anki's docs confirm desired retention 90% is the recommended default and >97% is unworkable.
verified_facts.evidence: https://docs.ankiweb.net/deck-options.html: desired retention "default is 90%, which offers a good balance of retention and workload", called "the most important setting in FSRS"; "above 97% the workload can be overwhelming". Same page confirms bury = delay until next day vs suspend = removed from study entirely, and lists the three sibling-bury options.

risks: Do NOT set enable_short_term:false. ts-fsrs switches to a completely different scheduler class in that case and my port diverges (measured: 2,969 mismatches in 5,792 transitions). With it true — the default — the port is exact across every config I tested.

Do NOT write a card's new state without also writing the review log in the SAME IndexedDB transaction. A partial write on an app backgrounded mid-review leaves a card whose stability no longer matches its history, which silently corrupts any future parameter optimisation.

FSRS elapsed time is whole CALENDAR DAYS computed in UTC (ts-fsrs uses Date.UTC on the y/m/d parts). Do not pass fractional days, and do not switch to local-date arithmetic — a user travelling across timezones would get off-by-one intervals. Note this is separate from the 4am day-rollover used for the daily LIMITS, which is deliberately local.

Do not clone a word into a second card when the user saves it from a video. Two cards for one word means two schedules, double reviews, and the learner concludes the app is broken. Add 'saved' to the existing card's decks array instead.

Do not auto-suspend leeches at the default threshold. Anki's own default is TagOnly for good reason; silently hiding the 8 words a learner struggles with most is the worst possible behaviour for a learning app.

Do not show Again/Hard/Good/Easy during the 'learn words' first-exposure screens. A beginner rating a word they met 4 seconds ago will overwhelmingly press Easy, seeding S=8.3 days on a word they cannot actually recall, and the card will not come back for over a week. Derive the first rating from an actual quiz response.

Do not attempt FSRS parameter optimisation in the browser in v1. It needs gradient descent over the full review history (realistically a WASM build of fsrs-rs) and does not beat the defaults until roughly 1,000+ reviews exist. Ship the export button instead.

Do not use FSRS-7 (the 34-parameter vector in fsrs-rs/src/inference_v7.rs). It adds a second memory trace (stability_fast), has no JS reference implementation, and is not the default anywhere — you would be shipping unvalidated math.

Fuzz makes intervals non-deterministic, so the number on the button must come from an unfuzzed preview (or you must reuse the exact fuzzed value you showed). Showing '5d' and then storing 6d looks like a bug to the user.

Burying must be reset at day rollover, not on app restart. Store buriedUntil as an absolute timestamp (nextDayStart) rather than a boolean, or a user who closes and reopens the app sees the sibling immediately.

With five levels x five card types, N1 alone can generate 10k+ cards. Do not materialise cards for words the user has not reached — create card rows lazily when a word is first introduced, and keep the 8,334 vocab notes as data. Otherwise the first IndexedDB population blocks the main thread on a phone.
Undo must restore a stored snapshot. FSRS is not invertible (mean reversion and fuzz both destroy information), so any attempt to 'un-schedule' by recomputing will drift.
